claims.text: Allergic rhinitis: not first-line; short-term relief of congestion only, not beyond 3–5 days. Oral decongestants (eg, pseudoephedrine) may cause tachycardia and hypertension
claims.quote: Decongestants are not recommended as a first-line therapy but can provide short-term symptomatic relief of nasal congestion. Prolonged use of intranasal decongestant sprays (eg, oxymetazoline, phenylephrine) can lead to rebound congestion (rhinitis medicamentosa), and oral decongestants (eg, a sympathomimetic such as pseudoephedrine) may lead to tachycardia and hypertension. Therefore, the use of decongestants is not recommended beyond 3 to 5 days.

claims.text: Nonallergic rhinitis: topical decongestants (eg, oxymetazoline) should be avoided; rebound congestion can follow 3 days of continuous use
claims.quote: Topical decongestants (eg, intranasal oxymetazoline) should be avoided for the treatment of rhinitis in general because they cause the vasculature of the nasal mucous membrane to lose its sensitivity to other vasoconstrictive stimuli—eg, the humidity and temperature of inspired air. Rebound congestion can result after 3 days of continuous use;
